Then he dragged me to a ground floor room that I had already rejected on WhatsApp video. He said this is only till 1 September and then the 5th floor will be mine. The kind of India we ignore
Last month, after a late night at work, I booked an auto to go back home. It was past 11, streets were half-empty, and I was half-dead from exhaustion. The auto driver was an older man, maybe late 50s, thin frame, tired eyes. Usually, I just plug in my earphones and zone out, but that day I didn’t.

We started talking. First, just small talk, traffic, weather, random stuff. Then I asked him casually, “Bhaiya, aap roz itna late tak chalate ho?” (Do you drive this late every day?)

He laughed, not in a happy way, but in a “what choice do I have” way. He said, “Bhaiya, do betiyan hain. Ek ke liye coaching fees deni hai, doosri ke school ka kharcha. Din mein 700–800 banta hai, usmein se aadha toh gas aur kiraya chala jaata hai. Raat ko chalata hoon taaki unki padhai na ruk jaye.”

I went silent. Here I was, cribbing about my corporate job, while this man was driving 14–16 hours a day so his daughters could have a shot at a better life.

Then he said something that has stuck in my head since that night:
“Gareeb aadmi sapne nahi dekhta apne liye, sirf apne bachon ke liye. Mere liye toh bas itna hai ki mujhe kal bhi chalane ki taaqat mile.”
(A poor man never dreams for himself, only for his children. For me, all I pray is that tomorrow I still have the strength to drive.)

By the time I reached home, I didn’t even feel like getting out of the auto. I gave him extra money, nothing life-changing, but he refused at first. Then he took it, folded his hands, and said, “Aapko bhi khuda taaqat de.”

I went upstairs, sat on my bed, and just kept thinking. Every day we complain about traffic, bosses, deadlines, Zomato deliveries being late. And at the same time, there are thousands of people around us who are literally breaking their bodies apart just so their kids don’t end up like them.

It humbled me. It made me realize how invisible these stories are, until you stop, listen, and acknowledge.

Maybe the biggest privilege we have isn’t money or English-speaking jobs. It’s the fact that we are allowed to dream for ourselves.

And I’ll never forget that one line from him:
“Gareeb aadmi sapne nahi dekhta apne liye.”

Feeling Lost Desperate for Help in My PM Job Search (NCR Relocation)
Hey everyone,

This is a tough post to write, but I’m out of options. I have more than 5 years’ experience managing projects, driving change, rolling out complex tech systems, and working side-by-side with developers and users. I’ve carried projects from start to finish, led teams, solved problems, and handled everything from planning to delivery. My experience spans tech, analytics, and operations across multiple jobs and companies.

**My Exp :-**

* **Project Manager (Product-led)** | 2.5 years | Led digital transformation, ERP rollouts, cloud migrations, team delivery
* **Co-Founder / Product Builder – Side Project** | 6 months | Built and launched a privacy-focused file sharing tool, gathered user feedback, shipped releases on tight timelines
* **Demand & Planning Lead Analyst – Swiggy(Instamart)** | 6 months | Improved demand forecasting and analytics for Instamart, collaborated across teams to optimize operations
* **Business Analyst** | 4 months | Hands-on analytics, system improvements, and process optimization
* **Data Analyst** | 2+ years (incl. KPMG US internship) | Created dashboards, automated pipelines, and drove business research

**I desperately want to switch to a Product Manager role and need to move to Gurgaon/Noida in 3 months to join my wife. I’ve put my heart into this:**

* Revamped my resume and LinkedIn to match PM requirements
* Applied to over 100 PM openings every platform I could find
* Invested ₹1,18,000 in a PM course to upskill and show my commitment

But the truth is, I haven’t received a single interview. Every day, I feel more anxious, more lost, and I’m starting to doubt my worth entirely. The silence is unbearable. I know I can deliver as a PM, but no one’s giving me a chance. It feels like my experience and effort mean nothing.

If anyone’s been through this, or if you have advice, leads, or even just honest feedback:

* How do I break through, make someone actually notice me for a PM job?
* Are there NCR recruiters, platforms, or companies that see beyond buzzwords and titles?
* Any raw, real tips for making this transition?

Please anything at all, a connection, a resume review, even encouragement. I’m truly grateful for any response. Thanks for reading.

Swiggy's unfair cancellation fee, but shout-out to Zishan
Hey, just had to share this absolutely mind-numbing experience with Swiggy tonight. I ordered food for my guests, and what followed was a comedy of errors that left me with hungry guests and a serious rage quit moment.

It all started when the delivery partner assigned to my order met with an accident. I called him to check on the status, and that's when he told me what happened. I felt really bad for him and, of course, understood why he couldn't deliver. After that, I immediately tried to contact Swiggy customer care, which took a while.

Once I finally got on a call with them, the agent was incredibly rude and ended up cutting the call on me. Unbelievable. I then tried my luck on the chat platform, where I got a hold of a support agent. I tried to cancel the order, but to my shock, they told me there would be a 100% cancellation fee. Seriously? It's not my fault the delivery guy had an accident, and it's not my fault the delivery was now impossible. But sure, I'll pay for the privilege of a failed delivery.

I decided to be patient and asked them to assign a new partner. A new partner was assigned, but surprise, surprise... he wasn't moving. I kept messaging the agent, who would disappear for 5 minutes at a time and then reply with a generic message. My guests were getting antsy, and I was getting seriously frustrated.

After some more back and forth, the agent finally told me the new partner had reached the restaurant. Great, I thought. Maybe now things will move. Nope. The restaurant hadn't even started preparing the food yet! The order was already delayed by more than 20 minutes at this point. I was essentially being punished for a string of failures that had nothing to do with me.

The food was still not on its way, my guests had given up and started eating biscuits. I'll be honest, I had completely lost my patience. But I have to give credit to the chat agent, Zishan. He was in total patience throughout the entire conversation. In the end, he managed to get me a 70% refund back, which was better than nothing.

This is the worst customer service I've experienced. How is it fair to charge a customer a 100% cancellation fee when all the delays and issues are on their end? Despite my awful experience with the call agent and the terrible policy, I do want to appreciate the help Zishan provided.

Has anyone else had a similar experience with Swiggy's ridiculous policies and terrible support? Let me know, I'm genuinely curious if this is a common issue.

If anyone wants to see the screenshots as proof, feel free to DM me.

Some experiences in Bangalore that shook me and some that touched my heart
I will just post a compilation of both heartwarming as well as negative interactions I had in Bangalore over the past few days working as a Zomato delivery partner.   
(Pardon my grammar and narration style for any mistakes or inconsistencies)

I was mired in some deep personal issues relating to divorce and lots other and had to quit job back in March. (Big time regret). Now I am unable to get any opportunities and hence decided to join Zomato to earn a livelihood until i land a decent job. here are some of the experiences that hurt me and some that touched me:

 **1. The rude lady**: After picking my order from the restaurant, I reached the location on time and reached the customers doorstep. There was no response even after ringing the bell. So I gave her a call and she started yelling at me for being in the wrong location. She called me "incompetent" and told me that I cannot even do a simple job like delivery.  
My English had a slight accent as well and she picked it mid way and passively mocking my accent with someone in the background as I pronounced it as "dɪˈlɪv(ə)ri" and she started highlighting it to her friend saying the "the dɪˈlɪv(ə)ri person couldn't find the location" and all. Somehow mentioned the location as a parlour and I made my way to there which was 1.5km from her given location.

Apparently she ordered some drinks to parlour but ended up ordering it to her home address. I didnt reason with her much, but just let her know what had apparently happened. She just told it might have been an app issue and left. No sorry, nothing. I exchanged a friendly smile and left.

**2.** **The chain snatch incident**: On my way to pick up an order, a cow jumped in front of me from my blind spot and in order to avoid a collision, I tried evading and fell on the road. Luckily the speed wasn't much, but i ended up bruising my knees and feet badly. My feet got stuck in the wheel alloy and from that day I am limping. A few people who were standing in the roadside were quick to respond, helped me up and parked my bike on the side. Those were some genuinely good people. 

I was so pissed off that people are letting their cattle loose on a highway but suddenly I felt it. Someone was trying to pull mu gold chain. My chain was tangled with the waterproof mobile pouch which I was wearing across my neck and as the person pulled it, i could quickly feel my phone lift up a bit. I immediately held my chain and looked back unable to figure who it was since there were a lot of people assembled around me. I was bleeding, I was in pain, I was high on adrenaline, but this incident really shook me. I swiftly took off and left the place en-route collect my next order.

**3.** **The very kind security person**: It was raining badly and I wasn't getting any orders. SO i thought to settle and await an order in a fast paced food spot. There were quite some restaurants there very adjacent to each other. I parked my vehicle and was limping to shelter and this old man saw me limping from a distance. He ran all the way to me and told me not to strain much, just let him know the order number and he will collect it on behalf of me.

I was so touched by the kind gesture of this man. I let him know that I haven't had any order yet and was just heading for a tea. I was feeling so overwhelmed my this kind gesture. 

4. **A mean bunch**: I reached the drop location and called the person and they let me know that they resided in the 5th floor. I looked up to see that they waved their hands to come to the top. I was limping, but in no way I was slow. I limped all the way to the top and i could hear the ladies talking in Malayalam where once girl was asking the other in Malayalam if that Limp legged Ma\*\*\*\*(cuss word in malayalam) hasn't come yet and the other person replied back to her saying that by the time that Ma\*\*\*\*(cuss word in Malayalam), it will be night.  
In no way I was slow. I was walking in the same pace as any normal human do. I felt bad, but this is how it is. Everyone was things so fast these days. I immediately showed up and suddenly it dawned on them that i might have heard them. I pretended as if I dint understand their language, proceeded to exchange a casual smile, handed their package and left.

5. **An angel of a lady**: I was heading to a delivery and as I crossed the road, I saw an old man with a walking stick struggling to put his chappal on. I without any hesitation bend down and helped him with it. He gratuitously told something in Kannada (which i didn't understand at all, but it made me feel happy).   
I proceeded to the 1st floor for the delivery where this lady was already standing in the corridor to collect the order. She collected the older and told me that i was a very good man. Apparently she she saw me helping the old man. I thanked her for being so nice and she invited me for a lunch. I lied to her saying that I did had my lunch just now only and thanked her for her benevolent gesture. Still she gave me some lime water and asked if I need anything else for my travel like snacks and all. I again lied to her that I am finishing my shift and left.

Her beautiful smile stayed with me. A lot of people has been mean to me in different ways, but never have my eyes turned wet. But now I as I drove to the next pickup location, I felt warm drops of tears rolling down my cheecks. Guess I could take all the hate in this world, But I am not used to getting love or people being nice to me.

6. **A very chill and open-minded guy**: It was late in the evening. My phone was already running out of charge. So as I reached a customer location, I asked the person if he could plug in my phone for charge for a good 5 minutes. This guy agreed and he invited me into his place. I told him i was good standing outside, but he insisted, made me sit, offer some water and before leaving even offered me that sweet peanut candy.  
I left that place with a feeling of warmth and happiness in my heart.

7. **The entitled lady**: I had a delivery at  facility which I believe was some sort of quarters or hostel facility for medical students/Doctors. The security wasn't allowing delivery person inside and asked me to call the concerned person. I called the person and waited for a good 10 minutes. It also started drizzling lightly. It was already 10 mins, I followed up again with a call to see that her phone was busy. I tried again to get shouted at asking why cant you wait a bit?

Now the drizzle has turned into a full blown rain and that too subsided after 5 mins back to a drizzle. Now this lady stepped out from the facility. Now it was nearing 20 mins. Guess  I should have reported to customer care already, but I gave her a call again. I realised that she was the one who exited the facility now and she is stalling talking to someone while making me wait in this cold rain. Again after a few minutes once she finished the call, she came and picked up my order.

No excuses for stalling, no apologies, not even an acknowledgement. Came and collected the package as if the entire purpose of my birth was to wait for her and then left just like that.

These experiences has really been a life-changer for me. They have really taught me a lot and reminded me of how good my life was when i just worked on weekdays in an A/C cabin with full blown facilities. I c consider each and every experience as a precious gem that is molding and shaping me into a better person with grit and resilience. 

But deep down I still wish the world would have been a better place with more nice people in it.

Am I the selfish and wrong one here?
Asking the Mumbai peeps as i feel you folks are much more modern, sensible and aware about this stuff.


——
So my GF(or ex now) is 26 and i am 29. I earn like 10x more than her. (Not bragging but to give you proper context).

content:
Mumbai and its rains: a humanitarian crisis?
I have lived here for only 3 years; and the hustle during monsoons is something that awes me till today. In Chennai; the entire city slumbers and takes a sabbatical if it has rained continuously for 3 hours. You can show up late to work or call in wfh. We used to have cyclones; and as a medical intern, we used to let our Dayscholar batchmates take the day off while we battled with our umbrellas through the flood and covered their duties as well. Nevertheless, duties were light. Only people who REALLY needed to come to hospital came, the rest had the good sense to stay home. Swiggy and zomato would say “sorry, we’re not taking orders at the moment”. If you are out of milk/sugar/need a hot meal- you gotta go ask your neighbours or the local shop like a normal person.


We still functioned. But we cut down on the non essential stuff. Lives are lost in the rains, and we know. Electrocution, infections, lack of transport. We spent the time to take care of each other and ourselves. We weren’t bothered about hustles, and making 5-10 rs. 
Maybe this hustle culture is vital for you as a city. Maybe, with your longer monsoons, this city does fall if you cut corners for the monsoons. Mumbai tries its best to function the same, whether it is raining cats and dogs or not. But it is a sign of capitalistic decay nonetheless. Perhaps, for the benefit of the safety of the person in front of you, we could scale back our dependence on goods and services for a day. Have ghar ka khichdi instead of chilli chicken on swiggy. Not go for a jog through the flood, even if that means we end up with a slight pooch for the next month. Relieve our dogs nearer to our homes and pick up their poo; instead of putting on wet boots and raincoats on them to soil the roadside, contaminating the waters that the rest of the city walks through. And take a goddamn nap while we are at it.

Beware: Is this a new online delivery scam happening in Mumbai and surrounding areas?
https://preview.redd.it/k5pyjbubsdgf1.jpg?width=1078&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=867ef19a351fdf6748e12e72f51d83d6ba3fd517

For context, last Saturday on 24th of July, I received an SMS from Shiprocket that some order has been picked up to be delivered to my address, from some seller in Thane.

I order many products online from Amazon, Flipkart, some independent sellers etc. But this specific message caught my attention because i couldn't recall placing any order in the first place. In fact I was traveling and on a family holiday and if I ordered something I would most certainly remember (all of us do, don't we?). But anyway I ignored that message thinking that must have been some kind of a mistake or a technical glitch.

Fast forward to today 1st of August, I got another message from Shiprocket that the same order was now out for deliver. So I logged in to Shiprocket app using my phone number to which I was receiving these updates, and to my surprise, there was indeed an order listed that was out for delivery through Bluedart. And within a couple of hours, a Bluedart guy came to place with a courier and said that it was a COD order for the amount of Rs 700. This was the moment I realized somebody's trying to scam me. Because my Amazon and Flipkart orders are usually pre-paid. I only order Swiggy and Zepto orders on COD because of my past experience where Swiggy, Zepto folks delay orders when they are pre-paid or give lame excuses not to deliver to my doorstep and ask me to come down in the parking or something (anyway, that's a story for another day).

The point is, ordering on COD from independent sellers who use Shiprocket is not something I normally do. So I refused to accept the delivery and the delivery guy left.

So what was this all about? Here's what I think happening and I am sure this is not happening to just me. This appears to be an elaborate, well thought-out scam.

\- First, a scammer will book Shiprocket and create a fake order. May be an empty box or something. I don't know how much Shiprocket costs but it shouldn't be too much including COD charges.

\- Shiprocket will route the order through their logistics partner (Bluedart in my case)

\- Bluedart will attempt a delivery and collect COD payment (which then goes to Shiprocket, and to the scammer).

If you ask Bluedart who is the sender, Bluedart says it was Shiprocket. This kind of protects scammer's identity so it makes perfect sense for them to book Shiprocket than to book Bluedart directly. And if you try to reach Shiprocket then IVR would tell you to connect with the seller directly. But how if the seller doesn't even exist?

In my case the seller information (on Shiprocket) included a website (which I didn't want to open - but I did) URL which did not point to any valid website. The domain wasn't connected to any website at all, Google search didn't return anything on the website either. So how exactly am I supposed to have placed an order in the first place? And even if I did, these orders require an email address, and Shiprocket generally sends email updates too. But in this case i didn't receive any email notifications too. So clearly, all scammer did was use my mobile number and address.

But how did they get that information? Now that's something to think about. While I don't blame Shiprocket, and I certainly don't blame Bluedart here, I think Shiprocket has messed things up somewhere. The database from Shiprocket is getting leaked maybe, or maybe it's from some other service altogether. I don't know for sure, but clearly our numbers and address details are getting leaked by "someone" (seller, logistics) - but who?

If you accept the order, you will pay COD, it will then go to scammer. So scammer has a clear profit margin, the amount he receives is at least 3x of what he must have paid Shiprocket. If you don't accept the order, the scammer faces losses. But I think they are taking chances nonetheless. Out of 10, even if 7 take the bait, they win. And that's what seems to be happening.

Whatever the case may be, please be careful. DON'T ACCEPT ANY DELIVERY YOU DIDN'T ORDER (COD OR OTHERWISE). What do you think about this? Have you faced anything like this?

Hi everyone,

I want to share something disturbing that happened to me and a friend on Friday (in Kurla, Mumbai) while ordering food via Swiggy.

I ordered from a restaurant using Swiggy. Since it was the first day of Shravan, I ordered a veg grilled sandwich for myself and a chicken shawarma for my friend. The order took around 1 hour — which was fine.

I’m sharing this here because: 1.	This is not just a refund issue — it’s about respect for religious practices and basic food safety. 2.	My friend could’ve seriously choked or been injured. 3.	Companies like Swiggy need to be held accountable beyond just “we’ll refund you, now go away.”

I’m not looking to defame anyone — but I do believe people should be aware. And I hope @swiggy_in sees this and takes real action.

Are Hyderabad's white-collar jobs walking into a 2030 apocalypse? (IT + others)
People around me still believe white-collar jobs = safe, guaranteed future. IT especially gets flexed as untouchable. But when you zoom out, there are multiple storm clouds gathering  not just AI.
Look around Hitech City, Gachibowli, and all the glass towers  they were built on IT salaries paid in dollars and euros.

For 20+ years, Hyderabad’s economy has thrived on what I call “burger money”:

A $10 burger lunch in the US became ₹800 here.

Dollar risk  : The U.S. dollar isn’t vanishing tomorrow, but de-dollarization and currency diversification are already happening. If the dollar loses some dominance, India’s IT hubs won’t get the same easy inflow of strong foreign money.

Multipolar world : Outsourcing was built on Western money. If trade shifts to local currencies (BRICS+, Gulf, Asia), salaries will benchmark lower. A U.S. client paying in dollars buys you 40 LPA, but a Russian or Brazilian client paying in weaker currency may give you “8 LPA” for the same work.(Dollar devaluation : as trust erodes, the 15-burger” pay scales will shrink.,)

In an age where convenience is just a tap away, food delivery apps like Swiggy have become essential for millions across India. They promise ease, speed, and reliability—but what happens when they fail, repeatedly, and without accountability?

Recently, I had an experience that not only left me hungry but also deeply disappointed with the level of service and disregard for customers that Swiggy displayed.

The Experience: A 2-Hour Wait for... Nothing

It all began with a simple order—nothing fancy, just a regular meal from a nearby restaurant. Placed the order on Swiggy and received the usual confirmation. Estimated delivery time: 45 minutes. Reasonable. I waited patiently.

An hour passed. Then another. No update. No delay notification. No message from the delivery partner or Swiggy support.

After two long hours, I finally decided to call Swiggy support myself. And that’s when the real shock came: the order had been canceled. No explanation. No refund initiated yet. No apology unless asked for. And worst of all, no notification—if I hadn't called, I would still be waiting.

Lack of Transparency and Communication

What’s most frustrating about this ordeal isn’t just the delay. It’s the complete breakdown in communication. Swiggy, a platform that boasts real-time tracking, instant chat support, and “quick resolutions,” failed on all fronts:

No automatic cancellation message

No real-time update or apology

No proactive refund initiation

No compensation for time lost


This isn’t just poor service—it’s negligent.

A Pattern of Failures

Sadly, this isn’t an isolated incident. Scroll through social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter), Reddit, or Instagram, and you’ll see thousands of users with similar complaints. Stories of hour-long waits, cold food, missing items, delayed refunds, or support chats that go nowhere.

Many have even noted that customer support often uses template responses with no real resolution offered—clearly indicating a shift from customer care to damage control.

Where is the Accountability?

Swiggy’s business model depends on the trust of customers and the cooperation of restaurant partners. But it seems they’re more focused on aggressive marketing and expansion than fixing the cracks in their system. When a company as large as Swiggy fails to deliver on the very basic premise of their service—food delivery—it raises questions about priorities.

Why was the order delayed for 2 hours before being canceled? Why wasn’t the customer informed? Why is the burden on the customer to follow up?

Update on the experiment of being a Swiggy rider to collect my own orders.
So Swiggy has caught up with me, and self orders have a penalty of 45 rupees.

Swiggy seems to be checking this via Phone number being the same.

I kinda expected to rack up lots of penalties during my experimenting phase so it was kinda expected but now I know what to avoid 

Now in my opinion is it worth it signing up to be one, in short the answer is no for the majority of people.

But I go to insane levels of frugality. 

What's my plan here. 

I currently have over 6 accounts on swiggy with the one subscription, The reason I do this is cause I can check prices on items on swiggy over multiple accounts, there are slight differences in coupons, also some accounts get free money on Swiggy Instamart, speaking of Instamart prices for the same item actually differs per account so it's good to check a number of accounts before finding the best way. Also I can use certain card offers again having multiple accounts.

Also another reason I have so many Swiggy one accounts is cause I can get  the mariott bonvoy offer again and again for those who don't know about it, it's an offer through which you get 200 free Swiggy money (for those trying to get it again and again read the terms and conditions on account activity before you do so)

Also its easy to spin up Swiggy one accounts(I know it's restricted to two per device, don't come at me saying that)

Now my plan is to order from numbers other than the one I registered for Swiggy rider with.

Now coming to the question is it worth it.

Yes and no, like I said for most people nope.

I place like over 60 orders a month and I will be using this only for 5-6 orders a month, the reason merely being convenience, I will only do orders within walking distance and when I am not feeling lazy.
So even if do a ton of orders a month the only ones I would be comfortable picking up would be around 5-6 a month.

I am looking at around getting 120 rupees a month.
Is it worth it? Well 120 rupees is kinda nothing to me but you have seen the levels of frugality I go to.
So it's kinda free money. By tipping I guess I will get cashback too. But eitherways I spend a ton of money on swiggy and it will help me save a tiny bit.

Over 90% of my expenses a month are on gift cards just so I can save a bit of money, I literally pay at every store with GVs.
